thread:
SRE-Bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — kv-cache fragmentation surge detected in region tokyo-prod. p95 latency jump 3.1x, error rate increased. Alert: KV-FRAG-3661122334.
Maya: i'm oncall. seeing the alert graphs now. who pushed the contbatch change earlier? :eyes:
Carson: that was my canary earlier this morning, rollout to 30% at 02:15UTC. logs show repeated arena allocations failing then falling back to slower path. a bunch of small allocations causing slab blowup.
Dmitri: can you paste the malloc error snippet?
Carson: sure — from the worker logs:

```
2026-03-15T02:47:12Z worker-17 ERROR runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (cuMemAlloc)
backtrace: .../runtime/arena.cpp:221 allocate_slab()
KVCache::alloc( size=2048 ) -> arena_fragmentation -> fallback_free -> slow_path_alloc
```

Carson: also seeing continuous batching counts spike, batch sizes up 4-5x, KV cache hitrate drops as fragmented arenas can't satisfy prefix allocations.
Lina: rolling partially back the contbatch config is low-friction; we can also reduce max_batch_tokens to lower tail pressure. which one faster?
Maya: do quick mitigation: reduce batch caps first, canary rollback if needed. we want least customer impact.
Carson: applying temp hotfix: set MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=2048 and CONT_BATCH_WINDOW=12ms on tokyo pool via admin API. running curl command now:

```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/pools/tokyo/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"max_batch_tokens":2048,"cont_batch_window_ms":12}'
```

Carson: applied to 100% of tokyo pool in ~90s. metrics: batching spike reduced, p95 latency trending down.
Product-Ops: customer impact check — Support flagged 9 customers with degraded responses, 3 with errors (502). Escalated to account owners.
Maya: good. now can we probe arena fragmentation and run compaction? we should avoid full process restarts if possible.
Dmitri: patch candidate: arena compaction pass that frees tiny slabs on low-util nodes. i'll push a non-disruptive canary to 5% after we stabilize.
Carson: ops note — memory telemetry shows >60% of free memory in tiny fragments <32KB. assembler shows allocator fallback rate spiking at 02:40.
Lina: started rolling canary rollback for contbatch to previous commit (v2.12 -> v2.11) on 20% of tokyo. command:

```
./deploy rollback --service kv-contbatch --to v2.11 --percent 20
```

Carson: canary rollback looks promising. p95 dropped ~35% on canary nodes. no regressions on throughput so far.
Support-Bot: automated customer-impact summary created: https://tickets.internal/incident/KV-3661122334 — 12 impacted sessions, 3 error escalations.
Maya: good work. going to notify oncall-handoff. i'll prepare a short incident summary for the night shift and hand over to Dmitri in 30min.
Dmitri: i'll take it. immediate next actions: 1) keep MAX_BATCH_TOKENS lowered for 6h, 2) run arena compaction canary, 3) snapshot and attach allocator telemetry, 4) postmortem draft tomorrow.
Carson: adding follow-ups — instrument per-slab age histogram, add alert for fragmentation ratio > 0.6, and schedule a patch to allocator heuristics (merge request MR#4872).
Lina: note: we should also add a temporary routing policy to divert to regional fallback if tokyo latency climbs again. ensures customer SLAs.
Product-Ops: notifying affected enterprise accounts with timeline and mitigation steps.
Maya: handoff: brief for night oncall @Dmitri — key facts: fragmentation spike after contbatch rollout -> arena malloc fallback -> batch fanout increases -> latency/errors. hotfix applied: batch caps lowered, partial rollback initiated, compaction canary planned. support tickets opened.
Dmitri: acknowledged, taking handoff. i'll monitor 02:30-08:30 JST. please post any logs or config diffs here.
Carson: saving relevant logs and commands to the incident thread. snippet of the diff we rolled back:

```
- cont_batch.max_inflight = 512
+ cont_batch.max_inflight = 256   # rollback
```

Carson: immediate status: stabilizing. will follow up with postmortem and timeline.
Maya: thanks team — if anything spikes again @channel. :thumbsup:
